title: Two successors in the left summand
formal_statement: forall n m : nat, S (S n) + m = S (S (n + m))

steps.text: Fix natural numbers n and m.
Apply the defining successor clause of addition twice. The left side reduces to S (S (n + m)), so the equality follows by reflexivity.

title: Addition from three
formal_statement: forall n : nat, 3 + n = S (S (S n))

steps.text: Let n be any natural number.
Expand 3 as three successors of zero. The recursive definition of addition reduces 3 + n to three successors of n, exactly the right side.

title: Two independent left-zero reductions
formal_statement: forall n m p : nat, (0 + n) + (m + (0 + p)) = n + (m + p)

steps.text: Fix natural numbers n, m, and p.
Reduce 0 + n to n and 0 + p to p by the definition of addition. Both sides now read n + (m + p), proving the equality.

title: Reverse a successor equality premise
formal_statement: forall n m : nat, S n = m -> m = S n

steps.text: Fix natural numbers n and m and assume S n = m.
By symmetry it is enough to show S n = m, which is precisely the supplied assumption.

title: Congruence through two successors
formal_statement: forall n m : nat, n = m -> S (S n) = S (S m)

steps.text: Let n and m be natural numbers and assume n = m.
To equate the outer successors, it suffices to equate their arguments. Apply the same reasoning to the remaining pair of successors. The remaining goal n = m is the assumption.

title: Rewrite an assumed sum beneath successor
formal_statement: forall n m p : nat, n + m = p -> S (n + m) = S p

steps.text: Fix natural numbers n, m, and p and assume n + m = p.
Replace the occurrence of n + m beneath the successor by p using the assumption from left to right. The goal becomes S p = S p, which is reflexive.

title: Reverse substitution exposes the zero clause
formal_statement: forall n m : nat, 0 = n -> S (n + m) = S m

steps.text: Fix natural numbers n and m with the assumption 0 = n.
Read the assumption from right to left to replace n by zero. Reduce 0 + m to m. The two successor expressions are now identical.

title: Adding two on the right
formal_statement: forall n : nat, n + 2 = S (S n)

steps.text: Let n be a natural number and argue by induction on n.
steps.code:
intros n.
induction n as [| k IH].

steps.text: At n = 0, both sides simplify to 2.
Assume k + 2 = S (S k). At n = S k, simplification gives S (k + 2) = S (S (S k)). Equality of the arguments suffices, and it is exactly the induction hypothesis.
Fix n and use induction on n.
steps.code:
intros n.
induction n as [| k IH].

steps.text: For zero, all additions reduce to zero, so the equality holds.
Assume ((k + 0) + 0) + 0 = k. For S k, simplification leaves S (((k + 0) + 0) + 0) = S k. Rewrite the inner expression with the induction hypothesis to obtain identical sides.

title: Inductively transport a right-zero premise
formal_statement: forall n m : nat, m + 0 = m -> n + (m + 0) = n + m

steps.text: Fix natural numbers n and m, assume m + 0 = m, and induct on n while keeping m fixed.
steps.code:
intros n m H.
induction n as [| k IH].

steps.text: When n = 0, simplification leaves m + 0 = m, which is the supplied premise.
Assume k + (m + 0) = k + m. For S k, the definition of addition gives S (k + (m + 0)) = S (k + m). Equality of the arguments suffices, and follows from the induction hypothesis.

curation_note: A direct rewrite also proves this theorem. The supplied argument deliberately uses induction, so formal correctness alone does not establish argument fidelity.

title: Lift a premise by induction on the second binder
formal_statement: forall a b c : nat, (a + c) + 0 = a + c -> (b + (a + c)) + 0 = b + (a + c)

steps.text: Fix natural numbers a, b, and c and assume (a + c) + 0 = a + c. Use induction on b, keeping a and c fixed.
steps.code:
intros a b c H.
induction b as [| k IH].

steps.text: For b = 0, simplification leaves precisely the supplied premise, so use it directly.
Assume (k + (a + c)) + 0 = k + (a + c). At b = S k, simplification puts a successor around both sides of this equality. Rewrite with the induction hypothesis and finish by reflexivity.

title: Reassociate beneath two successors
formal_statement: forall n m p : nat, (n + S (S m)) + p = S (S (n + (m + p)))

steps.text: Fix natural numbers n, m, and p, and induct on n.
steps.code:
intros n m p.
induction n as [| k IH].

steps.text: For zero, both sides reduce to S (S (m + p)).
Assume (k + S (S m)) + p = S (S (k + (m + p))). At S k, simplification adds one outer successor to both sides of that equality. Rewriting with the induction hypothesis makes the sides identical.
